notes: Questions to answer BEFORE building, distilled from findings/ledger.json. Each one cites the findings that taught it. `npm run brief` shows the ones whose classes touch the files you are about to change. The ledger gate requires an entry for every class and pattern that appears in the ledger.

RC-01.ask: What happens when this input, key, file, flag or directory is ABSENT? Absence must refuse or be declared — never read as success.
Which environment does this assume — repository top, PATH node, idle machine, git version, which git operations run hooks? Test the other one.
Does a hand-written list stand in for 'all' (directories, keys, codes, commands)? Enumerate from the source instead.
Can the same thing be reached by two names (symlink, hard link, relative path, case alias)? One name must be the only one.

RC-03.ask: Is a match judged on the captured text alone? Judge it in context: what surrounds it, and what the capture swallowed.

RC-04.ask: Are you listing cases where a structural rule exists (prefix lists, name lists)? Prefer the rule; test the shapes the list misses.

RC-05.ask: Which inputs come from someone else — the agent under test, operator text, hand-edited files, repository state (.git, replace refs), a shipped verifier? Each crosses a trust boundary: validate, escape, or do not trust it.
Can a caller-supplied id collide with an object key (__proto__, constructor)? Use own keys only.
Can the party this gate constrains perform the step that clears it (settle its own reconciliation, normalize its own path)? A person must.

RC-06.ask: Was this tried only on the canonical layout and friendly samples? Add the stranger's layout (relative paths, subdirectories, unusual git config) and a benign corpus.

RC-07.ask: Is a required step enforced only by rule text? Make the gate or the audit run it, and make a test fail when it is missing.

RC-08.ask: Does this write or value carry a meaning beyond its scope — a timestamp that means 'confirmed', a lock that a manual override bypasses? Classify every write.

RC-10.ask: Is every sentence you add to docs, specs or packs backed by a test that fails without it? Read it back against the code, not the intent.

RC-12.ask: Does the check fail for the reason it names, and only that? Put the bug back and watch it go red; no stopwatch; a positive control.
Was the judge different from the writer (another model, a fresh clone)?
Can this test actually observe what its name claims — does the race overlap, does the attack reach a live target? Add the control that proves it.

RC-09.ask: If this one unit (a frame, a case, a file) fails, does the whole run fail with it? Isolate it: the unit gets a named failure, the rest carries on.

fail-open-absence.ask: Delete it and run again: does the outcome still read PASS? If yes, the check is optional — make it required or declare why.
